per input line on stdout.

    # helpers
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    def load_value(buf, mem, addr, width):
        """Byte-wise: youngest own-buffered store covering the byte wins,
        otherwise shared memory.  Assembled little-endian."""
        val = 0
        for i in range(width):
            a = addr + i
            b = -1

            for j in range(len(buf) - 1, -1, -1):
                sa, sw, sv = buf[j]

                    b = (sv >> (8 * (a - sa))) & 0xFF
                    break
            if b < 0:
                b = mem[a]
            val |= b << (8 * i)
        return val

    def read_mem(mem, addr, width):
        val = 0
        for i in range(width):
            val |= mem[addr + i] << (8 * i)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Exhaustive enumeration of terminal observable outcomes of the
mixed-width buffered (TSO-like) machine described in the task.

Requests are newline-delimited JSON objects on stdin; one JSON response
object per request line is written to stdout, in order.

Machine summary (every transition is atomic, including multi-byte ones):

  * state: per-thread program counter, per-thread FIFO store buffer,
    shared memory, per-thread list of observed load/xchg values.
  * execute (per thread, program order):
      store  -> append (addr,width,value) to own FIFO, pc+1 (memory untouched)
      load   -> byte-wise: youngest own buffered store covering the byte wins,
                otherwise shared memory; assembled little-endian into an
                unsigned value, appended to own observations, pc+1 (non blocking)
      fence  -> enabled only with an empty own buffer, pc+1
      xchg   -> enabled only with an empty own buffer; atomically read the
                shared-memory value, append it to own observations, write the
                supplied value to those bytes, pc+1
  * drain: the oldest store of any non-empty buffer becomes globally visible
    (all of its bytes at once) and is removed from the buffer.  Draining stays
    enabled after the issuing thread has finished.
  * terminal: all programs finished and all buffers empty.  No fairness
    assumption: the set of finite terminal executions is what is enumerated.
"""

import json
import sys

sys.setrecursionlimit(1000000)

STORE, LOAD, FENCE, XCHG = "store", "load", "fen
